Local tool · single developer

Show a coding agent exactly where the UI drifted

Paste a screenshot of the interface as built, drag a rectangle over what's wrong, and write a sentence about it. What comes out is one image an agent can act on — because a drawn rectangle is a far higher-bandwidth way to say here than any description of a location.

📌 On a phone, press and hold any screenshot below to save it to your photos.
1

Paste the interface as built

Drop or paste a screenshot anywhere on the page. Nothing is uploaded — the tool runs on your machine and the image never leaves it.

2

Mark what drifted

Drag a rectangle over each divergence and write what's wrong beside it. Attach the intended design on the right and both sides travel together. Each region gets a numbered pin, shaped like a Figma comment so it can't be mistaken for part of the screenshot underneath.

3

Hand it over

One image carries everything: the capture on the left, the intended design on the right, and every note on a card beside its pin. The type is set larger than the interface underneath on purpose — an agent's vision pipeline shrinks an image this wide before reading it, and the notes have to survive that.

The second button writes that image to disk and puts this on your clipboard, so one paste gives the agent the picture and the words at once:

The report image is at ~/reports/report-2026-08-16T12-48-33-256Z.png.
